A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the mean number of events per person in any open population is equal to the sum of the product of the age-specific rates and the expected age-specific counts.
the Nelson-Aalen estimators are the appropriate estimators of the expected total count per person in any open population, and that they are unbiased, consistent, and asymptotically normal.

the mean number of events in an age-dependent Poison process is estimated by the cumulative age-specific rate, even if the events are not generated by a Poisson process, and even if the population is open.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the TFR and GGR can be used as estimates of the expected number of children per woman even when the underlying birth process is not Poissonian.
the Nelson-Aalen estimate of the cumulative hazard of a Poisson process, when the number of units in the population is known, is a good estimator of the expected count per individual.

if the population is large enough, and if the events of interest are not strongly clustered within individuals, then the empirical mean number of events per person is a good estimate of the expected number.
